title: What the next capture of the official availability report must look like, pinned before it is taken
pinned_from: nfl-availability-desk/data/availability_snapshot_2026-11-15.csv via engine/audit.py - no number here is typed
why: The brief's alarm: 'give every scraper an expected row count and required fields so a source-schema change fails the build instead of quietly returning zeros.' A source change that halves the rows must fail loudly, and a passing build must mean the row count and the field set were checked, not assumed.

designation_coverage_pct.note: floor is a tripwire, not a target: coverage legitimately varies by day of week, so a value below 35% means the capture lost its designation column, not that the league changed

tolerance.rows_by_club_delta_allowed: 0 for a same-week re-read; +/-4 for a different week of the season (a bye week legitimately removes 4 sections)
tolerance.vocab_additions: an unlisted value is always a FAIL: the official table has printed exactly three practice statuses and three game labels since the capture began, so a fourth string means the source changed

known_gaps: the 4 clubs on bye publish no section: a capture that shows 32 sections has been padded by someone
game_status is blank on about half of all rows in the official report by design; 'blank' must never be rewritten to 'Available' (see flag on the readiness register R-13)
checked_by: engine/drift.py, invoked by .github/workflows/nfl-availability-desk.yml and by engine/verify_site.py
